title: Es tut mir leid
desc: An apology has to name the thing
setting: By the weir, loud enough that you both have to speak up, three days later than it should be.

options.es: Es tut mir leid für die zwei Tage.
options.en: I am sorry about the two days.
options.feedback: Sorry for what. A general es tut mir leid reads as evasion here; the thing has to be named.
She will wait. Not to punish you: she is waiting for the second half of the sentence.

options.en: I have thought about it a lot.
options.feedback: A good opening and not an apology. It is the sentence she uses, and she uses it before something.

options.es: Der Samstag war nicht das Problem.
options.en: The Saturday was not the problem.
options.feedback: Correct, and knowing which thing to apologise for is most of the work.

options.en: I am sorry about that too.
options.feedback: Adding items to the list is not the same as finding the right one.
She was. She was more right about the other thing, and that is what she is waiting for.

steps.speaker: Selina
steps.es: Ich war auch zu still. Ich mache das immer.
steps.en: I was too quiet too. I always do that.

options.feedback: Her own move, given back. Not ist schon gut, which would make what she just said smaller.
She did not offer it to be waved away. Letting it stand is the respectful thing here.
Warm and it does not shrink it. Slightly big for the register and it lands.
That is the end of it. No big sentence, no ceremony: a small ordinary thing done together.
Asking reopens it. Nobody here says the sentence that ends it, and Kaffee was the sentence.

options.es: Ja. Und dann muss ich noch etwas sagen.
options.en: Yes. And then I have one more thing to say.
options.feedback: If it is a new thing, fine. If it is the same thing again, it will undo the last half hour.
